status: FINAL. All 13 files are in place.
notes: Every file is a transparent-background SVG in three colours: black #000, orange #f9452d, paper #f8eee8 (the page --bg). No raster, no text inside the art. Paper is a real fill, so the art works on cream and on the orange panel without blend modes.
display_em is [width, height] in em at the intended size (1em = 16px at 1440). At that size the outline is about 3.5px. Smaller is fine; keep art visible on phones.
Use with the width and height given here (viewBox units) so the layout holds. Decorative uses: alt="" and aria-hidden.
Inline the SVG only if you want to restyle it: paths sit in groups with class ink, paper or orange.

contact-camel-head.svg.role: head without lower jaw and ears; includes a short neck stub that ends in a round paper cap centred on neck.attach

contact-camel-jaw.svg.role: lower jaw with the black inside of the mouth

rotate_deg.sign: CSS rotate, positive closes the mouth

contact-camel-lid.svg.role: eyelid: paper almond over the eye with a black closing edge. Blink with scaleY 0 (open) to 1 (closed)

about-hero.svg.alt: The Brandle family photo: an orange camel resting its chin on a man in sunglasses, a woman with big wavy hair, and a white spotted camel nibbling her hair.
about-hero.svg.note: Cut flat by the left, right and bottom edges like a cropped photo. Clear space above the heads.

notfound.svg.alt: A lost orange camel standing on two legs with a rucksack, frowning at a map it is holding upside down.

work-hero.svg.alt: The two designers hang a big framed screen. He is on a step stool, she checks if it is straight, and the spotted camel is pulling one corner up with its teeth, so it is not.

screen.note: blank paper area inside the black frame, free for live content or a .mock__screen; the woman's head and raised hand overlap its lower right

about-story-1.svg.alt: The orange camel calmly eating the corner of a paper brief.
about-story-1.svg.beat: how we work: the brief (fixed quote before work starts). The sheet carries dummy bars, add any word as HTML on top.

about-story-2.svg.alt: A hand in an orange sleeve passing a big key with a tiny camel charm to an open hand.
about-story-2.svg.beat: the client owns the code and files
about-story-2.svg.note: Wide and short: 35.13em wide is about 15em tall. Centre it in the 35.13em x 37em slot or show it at full column width.

about-end.svg.alt: The spotted camel sitting upright in an office chair that is too small for it. The second chair is empty with an orange bomber jacket over its back.
about-end.svg.note: Made for the orange field: the jacket's orange merges with the ground and reads as line work. Also fine on cream.

blog-hero.svg.alt: The orange camel sitting cross-legged in round reading glasses, reading a large newspaper.

services-hero.svg.alt: The white spotted camel wearing a tool belt full of tools, a pencil behind its ear and a spirit level in its mouth.

contact_camel.coordinate_space: All five part files share one viewBox, 0 0 1594 1642. Stack them at the same position and size; every point below is in that space. Percent origin for CSS: x/1594, y/1642.

neck.direction: straight down from attach at rest
neck.how: two paths with the same d and round caps, starting at attach: black at width_outer under paper at width_outer - 2*outline. Units are viewBox units, scale with the art. The head's stub ends in a round cap centred on attach, so the head can turn about attach without a seam (checked to 12 degrees either way).

mouth.note: Put the middle of the card's right edge on hold_point, transform-origin 100% 50%, rotate(-14deg): the card then runs out to the left along the upper lip, left end lower. To make the card tilt up 8 degrees as in the spec, turn the whole head group by rotate(22deg) about head_pivot. The upper lip (head) covers the card's top right corner; the jaw closes on it from below at 22 degrees.

contact_camel.spots: three small spots on the cheek only; none on the neck stub, so neck spots are yours to add as ellipses
contact_camel.tested: rest pose, jaw at -5, 12, 16, 24 and 34 degrees, ears at -18 to 14, lid at 0, 0.5 and 1, head at -10, 6 and 12 degrees, on orange and on cream, at 420, 300, 240 and 120 px wide
known_limits: with the jaw closed past 16 degrees a small straight edge shows at the back corner of the mouth; the card hides it
ears turned more than 14 degrees toward each other open a hairline at the base

source.model: Google Nano Banana 2.1 at 2k with the hero still as reference; traced with potrace into three flat layers
